angles.drive: Spotting an opening is what you do first, before it is obvious to anyone. You carry less Wood than drive to spend on it, so you spot the far chance more clearly than the one already in your hand. Spot the near one as carefully, because it is the one within your reach.
angles.cost_self: Where you spot openings is always a little past where you stand. Since you want to be free more than settled, you spot what is far instead of taking what is in front of you. Take a near one too, because each far chance you spot costs you a chance already in hand.
angles.cost_others: You point out every opening you spot to whoever is near. Because the far chance holds you more than the near one, you are off spotting the next rather than finishing this with them. Finish this one first, since spotting the next takes a little from them, your attention on what you started together.

angles.drive: Starting comes easily to you, often before you have finished deciding. Moving is how you feel alive, so you start and learn rather than wait until you are sure. Start as freely as you do, and let one start run long enough to teach you its ending.
angles.cost_self: Whenever something new opens, you have started before asking what it will take. Starting feels like freedom and waiting like a cage, so you take the quick start ahead of the rest owed to you. Take the slow middle along with the start, because every quick start costs you the rest you never take.
angles.cost_others: You start things with other people in them, well before the thing is real. Since you need movement more than certainty, you start and move on and leave the middle to the people you brought in. Stay for one ending with them, because each start you share leaves them the middle to finish.

angles.drive: Giving comes more naturally to you than keeping, with money the clearest case. Since being generous keeps the world feeling wide, you give away a lucky month rather than put it aside. Give the way you always have and hold one part back, because what you keep is what the giving stands on.
angles.cost_self: Giving is your first answer to most things, and what you keep pays for it. Since being generous feels more like you than being careful, you give the extra ahead of putting any aside. Give one part of a good month to yourself, because the money you never keep is what giving costs you.
angles.cost_others: Whenever the people close to you run short, you give before being asked. Since giving keeps you freer than being owed ever has, you give outright rather than build anything shared. Let them give back once in a while, because your giving takes one small thing from them, the chance to be generous too.

angles.drive: Whatever is newest in front of you is the thing you chase hardest. There is more Wood in you than strength behind it, so you chase the fresh start ahead of the finish every time. Remember that the half-done thing behind you was once the new thing you chased.
angles.cost_self: Where you are now is rarely the thing you are chasing. Because staying feels like being stuck rather than being home, you chase the far plan with the hours the near one needed. Remember what every chase costs you, the venture already begun, and a half-finished venture pays nothing.
angles.cost_others: Chasing the next thing is how you stay alive. Since the new chance pulls you harder than the one you promised, you chase it and leave the unfinished half to your partner. Keep in mind that you promised them the middle as well as the start, whatever you are chasing now.

angles.drive: Spreading yourself across several things feels normal to you, and one thing alone feels like being caught. Your Wood outruns the strength carrying it, so you spread across every open option rather than let one go. Remember how thin you get, spread over all of them with only the one body.
angles.cost_self: You are spread among more things than your body keeps up with. Because letting go feels like losing rather than choosing, you spread yourself across every one of them and give each a tired version of you. Remember that you carry the tiredness home, and spread this thin you never get a full rest.
angles.cost_others: Whenever something new asks for you, you spread one slice thinner over all the people already holding one. Since closing an option feels like losing it, you spread across all of them rather than shut one. You know already that you hand your partner and family the same thin slice as everything else.

angles.drive: Unspent money feels less real to you than money already gone. Spending is how you keep life feeling open, so you spend an easy month rather than put any of it toward a month that waits. Remember that you will be the person the slow month happens to, with everything already spent.
angles.cost_self: Where money is concerned, you spend it sooner than you let it sit. Since spending feels like living and saving like waiting, you spend this month's money ahead of ever keeping any. You arrive in the thin month too, remember, with the money already spent and nothing kept.
angles.cost_others: You spend on the people around you before you spend on your own next month. Because spending on them feels better than keeping ever has, you spend to cover their short months rather than build a shared cushion. Remember that you spend their quiet months as well as your own.

angles.drive: Your effort naturally runs in several directions at once, and the directions feed each other more than they collide. Focus, as commonly preached, never fit you: your luck lives in the overlaps, where one venture waters the next. So you stopped apologizing for the branching.
angles.cost_self: The supplier from the first venture became the landlord of the second, and a customer from the second just introduced the third. On paper it is three businesses in two cities. In practice it is one root system wearing three names, and it feeds itself.
angles.cost_others: People who chase one goal at a time find your calendar hard to explain. You keep three ventures alive across two cities, and somehow the overlaps feed each other instead of colliding. Spreading is simply how opportunity finds enough doors to knock on.

angles.drive: Seeing the opening before others see the wall is your standing advantage. Where most people need proof, you need one walk past the site, and the plan assembles itself uninvited. Most of what you imagine stays imaginary. The fraction you build pays for the whole habit.
angles.cost_self: You walked past the empty lot once and the café appeared in your head, tables and all, a year before anyone else saw potential. By the time the neighborhood caught up, you had already moved on twice. Early is the only schedule you have ever kept.
angles.cost_others: Friends have learned to listen when you point at nothing and describe a business. Half your ideas sound absurd on the sidewalk and obvious five years later. The people who laughed at the first one quietly ask about the next.

angles.drive: Money moves through your hands easily, and it keeps coming back with interest of a kind no bank tracks. You give without counting, on instinct, and the instinct has been running a quietly profitable book for years without ever once being audited.
angles.cost_self: You covered the dinner without thinking, the way you seeded the friend’s shop and floated the cousin’s rent. Nobody kept a ledger, least of all you. Somehow the shop sends customers, the cousin sends leads, and generosity keeps turning out to be your best-performing account.
angles.cost_others: The word on you is generous, and the word travels further than money does. Doors open because you propped one open for someone else two years back. Tight-fisted people never see this economy at all, and they keep wondering how you afford your luck.

angles.drive: Starting is your genuine talent, and staying is the tax you keep finding ways around. Your energy is all spring and no autumn: everything gets planted, nothing gets brought in, and the finish line remains a rumor from other people’s lives.
angles.cost_self: Four projects, all around forty percent, none moving. The oldest one needed two weekends of work in March, and it is October, and those weekends went to the newest one, which has since also stopped. The finish line has never once seen you up close.
angles.cost_others: People have stopped asking how the projects are going, because the answer is always the same word, almost. Your talent was never the question. What they are waiting for, some more patiently than others, is a single finished thing to point at.

angles.drive: Adding commitments is a reflex you no longer notice, the way a hedge never notices new branches. Every yes seemed small at the moment of signing. The sum runs your life now, and the important thing keeps not happening inside a calendar too full to hold it.
angles.cost_self: There is no white space left in the calendar, and reading it honestly is uncomfortable: half the entries are things you volunteered for while already busy. Each one was one small yes. Together they are the reason the important thing keeps not happening.
angles.cost_others: From outside, your life looks impressively full, and people say so with admiration. Up close, the fullness has no center. Even your closest people book you two weeks out, and the thing you say matters most has not appeared on the calendar in months.

angles.drive: Your interest burns hottest at the start and moves on before results arrive, and the pattern is old enough to have its own shelf. Enthusiasm was never the missing ingredient in any of it. Week seven is, and week seven always has been.
angles.cost_self: The guitar got six good weeks, then the course got its six, then the market stall. Each one was the real thing while it lasted, and the shelf where they ended up is running out of space. Week seven has beaten you more often than any rival.
angles.cost_others: Friends now respond to your new obsessions with a warmth they privately ration, because they have met week seven. Nobody doubts the passion. They have simply watched enough six-week eras end to know the shelf, and never the stage, is where this one is headed too.
